subject.title: sessions.create fork path has no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete

question: Should this public cross-plugin `sessions.create` parent-link/fork ownership gap be fixed through the normal public issue flow, or redirected to security/advisory handling before repair automation?
rationale: Source inspection confirms a missing guard, but `SECURITY.md` asks for private handling of unpatched vulnerability PoCs while also treating trusted-installed plugins as part of the TCB, so automation should not choose the disclosure and release-handling path.

options.title: Route security first
options.body: Pause repair automation until a security owner decides advisory, privacy, and backport handling for this public report.

options.title: Approve narrow public fix
options.body: Treat this as a normal public gateway bugfix and patch the existing plugin-runtime ownership invariant with focused tests.

options.title: Treat as hardening only
options.body: If maintainers decide the trusted-plugin model means this is not a security boundary, keep it open as a normal session isolation hardening bug.

recommendation.title: Route security first
recommendation.body: Pause repair automation until a security owner decides advisory, privacy, and backport handling for this public report.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged session fork/control PR that introduced the current operator fork path and is the strongest recent routing signal for the security-boundary choice.
